stories.headline: Cyclone to trigger heavy rain in south Odisha
stories.title: Cyclone to trigger heavy rain in south Odisha
stories.summary: System likely to make landfall on Oct 28 morning somewhere between northAP and south Odisha coasts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bhubaneswar: The Odisha government on Saturday activated its disaster response and mitigation machinery as the well-marked low-pressure area was likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm and make landfall between the northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha coasts on the morning of October 28.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its latest bulletin, said the system over the Bay of Bengal was most likely to intensify into a depression on Saturday.
Thereafter, it is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression on October 25 and into a cyclonic storm by October 26 morning.

“Moving west-northwestwards, it would continue to intensify further and reach west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around the morning of October 28,” the national weather agency said.
The IMD Director General, Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, said the system is “likely to make landfall on the morning of October 28 somewhere between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha coasts”.

Keeping in view the impending calamity, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed the State’s preparedness and directed officials to prioritise public safety, evacuation and emergency response, stressing a zero-casualty objective.
He said the cyclone could affect Odisha, bringing heavy rainfall in southern and coastal districts along with gusty winds of 70-90 kmph.
Five districts -- Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri -- are likely to be the most affected, while significant rainfall is expected in other coastal districts, the Chief Minister said.
He directed authorities concerned to close schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in these five districts on October 28-29.
In other districts, the collectors will decide on closing schools and colleges based on the evolving situation, Majhi said.

Asserting that Odisha has experience in handling such disasters, the Chief Minister asked officials to shift people from vulnerable areas to safer locations, with special emphasis on moving elderly persons, patients and pregnant women to health centres.
Majhi said rescue teams of Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Fire Services have already been positioned in vulnerable places.

stories.headline: Bay of Bengal depression may become very severe cyclone before Andhra landfall
stories.title: Bay of Bengal depression may become very severe cyclone before Andhra landfall
stories.summary: Bay of Bengal depression may become very severe cyclone before Andhra landfall
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A Bay of Bengal depression is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast as a very severe cyclone.
Authorities have recalled fishing boats and alerted residents amid warnings of destructive winds and extreme rainfall.

A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression on Saturday and is likely to become a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on October 28, the India Meteorological Department said.
The system is expected to bring heavy rainfall to parts of Andhra Pradesh from October 26 to 29.
Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain alert and warn people in low-lying areas.
The depression was over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal at 5.30 pm on Saturday.

It was about 510 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman Islands, 820 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 910 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 1,020 km east of Machilipatnam and 1,100 km east of Bapatla, the Met Department said in a release.

The system is likely to move nearly southwards and strengthen into a deep depression before gradually turning west to northwest over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal by October 25.
It is then expected to continue moving west to northwest and develop into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26.
The system is forecast to become a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal around the morning of October 27.
It is likely to move northwestwards, intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around the morning of October 28.

The storm is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by late morning that day, with sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kmph and gusts of up to 140 kmph.

stories.headline: SEC removes three police officers over election conduct
stories.title: SEC removes three police officers over election conduct
stories.summary: The AP State Election Commission removes three police officers from election duties, including Chilakaluripet SI Priyanka for pushing former minister Vidadala Rajini.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The AP State Election Commission removes three police officers from election duties, including Chilakaluripet SI Priyanka for pushing former minister Vidadala Rajini.

Amaravati: The State Election Commission (SEC) has ordered the removal of three police officers from election-related duties over alleged lapses and misconduct during the ongoing local body election process, including sub-inspector Priyanka of Chilakaluripet, who was accused of pushing former minister Vidadala Rajini to the ground.

The SEC ordered the removal of Molakalacheruvu circle inspector Dastagiri and sub-inspector Ramakrishna in Annamayya district, citing alleged negligence during the nomination process and biased conduct.
In a separate action, it removed Chilakaluripet SI Priyanka following a review of video footage showing her confrontation with Rajini.
The incident occurred when YSRCP candidates arrived at Rajini’s residence in Chilakaluripet on Friday.
Police allegedly prevented them from entering the house, prompting the former minister to come outside and question the officers over the restrictions.
During the ensuing argument, Priyanka allegedly pushed Rajini, causing her to fall to the ground.
The incident triggered a political controversy, with the video drawing attention to the conduct of police personnel during the election process.
Following its review, the SEC ordered action against Priyanka.

stories.headline: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
stories.title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that “right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so”.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002.

NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for lying and furnishing a false declaration as Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable and the Election Commission’s nod was not needed.

Explaining the interplay between Section 125-A of Representation of People Act and Section 195(1) of the CrPC which says that no court shall take cognisance of any offences punishable under sections 172 to 188, including the offence of furnishing false information to a public servant, the top court held that Section 125A of RoP Act does not come within the ambit of Section 195 of CrPC and a court can take cognisance of a private complaint.
The court’s ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that “right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so”.

SC said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002, while Section 195 of CrPC was amended in 2006, and that the omission of the legislature to include Section 125-A of the RoP Act in Section 195 of CrPC was deliberate and no court would be barred from taking cognisance of an alleged offence under Section 125-A of the RoP Act, even on the complaint lodged by a private person.
“Should we read into Section 195 of CrPC a prohibition in respect of Section 125-A of the RoP Act also, apart from those expressly included?

If indeed it were the intention of the legislature that cognisance of any offence relating to furnishing of false information by a candidate in an affidavit with intent of being elected in an election (referred to in Section 125-A of the RoP Act) could only be taken if the complainant were a public servant, the same could have been provided by an amendment of Section 195, CrPC since Section 125-A of the RoP Act is of fairly recent origin.” SC also refused to give credence to the EC’s press note that it can take cognisance of such complaints and refer such matters to the relevant investigating authorities on a case-to-case basis.

Even though the ECI is supreme in its own sphere and has, indeed, issued guidelines/press notes based on its understanding of the statutory provisions, interpretation of statutes is primarily the task of the courts and such guidelines/press notes do not bind us,” the court said.
It said that Karnataka HC erred in holding that a private complaint cannot be filed for an offence under Section 125A of RoP Act which is punishable up to six months of jail term.
The HC had interpreted the provision solely upon reading the letter issued by the Election Commission of India on the issue which was rejected by the apex court.
